newsitem.title: USA: U.S. securities measure should cut red tape - ICI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. securities measure should cut red tape - ICI.

text.p: U.S. securities legislation signed Friday by President Bill Clinton should help reduce red tape in the mutual fund industry, according to the Investment Company Institute, a trade group.

"We expect (the measure) will be helpful and will be able to address the modernization of the regulation and duplication issue, so that the states and federal authorities are not duplicating their efforts," a spokesman for the group said.
The law reforms the regulation of mutual funds and gives the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission more money to supervise investment advisers.
Among the changes, it exempts securities offered by mutual funds from state regulations.
The ICI said it believed the legislation would yield savings for the industry and "this savings would be passed on to shareholders."
